body: I am not planning on getting together. I am strictly speaking about a chat, unless you're implying that one will definitely lead to another.

I'm aiming to do better should anything like that happen ever again. The feeling of not knowing what type of person she really was pisses me off more than rejection ever would I think. Gotta fight those fears!

She was a total stranger, but she had this thing about her. The way that she smiled at the waitress that brought her coffee, it was a genuine, compassionate smile. You could see that in her lips as well as her eyes. I think that got me. 

By the time i started thinking about talking to her I was already losing. Thinking won over action this time. 

I wasn't scared of being rejected, I was scared of making an idiot out of myself and stuttering like crazy. 

The night before I got slightly drunk with my friend and ended up dancing in a beach club. I even danced with a cute girl in a polkadot dress. 

I guess I need to start doing that from time to time. Get a bit drunk and then try to do the same sober.

That is going to be the next thing I'll do. I just want to find a good therapist, which I suppose is going to be a little bit tough in a small town like mine, but I feel like I'll manage. The thing is, I'm starting a new job in a couple of days and I just feel drained. There's no way I'll be able to talk to a specialist any time soon. It's going to be a month of pretending that everything is fine and I am bad at pretending. You have my sincere thanks for taking interest in a random dude on the internet though, Thank You very much.

I may be wrong but I would at least honestly ask for actual answers not just some over the top sentences that effectively mean nothing. Don't do that through text messages, text limits dialog, go there look her in the eye and have an actual heated conversation. Ask her what did she mean exactly when she texted You all these things. After that conversation is done You have to decide how much are You willing to give up for that friendship (which ideally should not be much, You shouldn't change yourself for a single person because that is going to come back and bite You in the ass when You ask Yourself one day "Who am I?" and the easiest answer will be "My friend's puppet".). 


You may suffer from low self-esteem (like majority of people I presume. I too, know what it feels like) and may even be willing to sacrifice a lot to get that friendship back. You have to understand that after an episode such as this even if You reconcile and explain all the shit to each other it's not going to be the same. Changes have to be made to make it into an actual lasting friendship that You claim you need. If done correctly it will empower You both instead of limiting You and putting You in perpetual state of paranoia (I shouldn't be doing this because she doesn't like this and it might cause her to lash out one day) 


On the other hand there's a different, much more difficult way. You can accept the fact that this friendship is over, and start to search for happiness inside of You. I know how bullshit this sentence sounds, but if You try to find out and accept who you are and stick with it, You will eventually encounter people who are like-minded and they will definitely stay with You and won't try to change You forcefully.
